title: DC-area forecast: Clearing skies tonight; pleasant and less humid Friday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Partly cloudy with decreasing humidity tonight and lows in the mid- to upper 60s.

What’s next? Friday is probably dry, but Saturday could feature persistent and widespread rain chances. Mostly 80s for highs into next week.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Partly cloudy this evening and overnight, with gradually decreasing humidity, as lows drop to the mid- to upper 60s. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Mostly to partly sunny, and likely dry during the day, with just a slight chance of a shower south of DC. Highs should be in the low to mid-80s with somewhat lower humidity (dew points in the mid-60s). Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Turning cloudier and more humid over time, and showers may develop, especially after midnight. Mid-60s to low 70s for lows. Confidence: Medium-High

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Temperatures remain close to or a bit below normal through the weekend. There's a chance of showers and storms both days, but particularly Saturday when there could be some heavier rain in a more widespread fashion. Highs mostly reach the low to mid-80s. Confidence: Medium

Humidity may fall further toward Monday, opening up the work week on a relatively nice note as sun rules and highs reach for the mid-80s. More low to mid-80 are a good bet into Tuesday and seemingly beyond. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 20

A torrential 1963 downpour set a rainfall record, triggering significant flooding, closing National Airport, and inundating homes and businesses across the region.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Temperatures are a little lower than yesterday but it's a good deal more humid and there's a storm threat. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
